items.s: Health education is planned learning that helps people choose and maintain behaviour likely to protect wellbeing.

items.q: “the proportion of those exposed to a common source who become ill during an outbreak” is the definition of
o: Endemic
Attack rate
Prevalence
Notifiable disease
items.s: Attack rate is the proportion of those exposed to a common source who become ill during an outbreak.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Air pollution?
o: contamination of the air by smoke, dust or gases at levels that harm people
the collection and final handling of solid household waste in a way that does not breed pests
measures that reduce or destroy the insects and other carriers of infection
the accepted requirements for space, light, ventilation and drainage in a dwelling
items.s: Air pollution: contamination of the air by smoke, dust or gases at levels that harm people. The other options describe Housing standard, Vector control, Refuse disposal.

items.q: “the indirect protection of unvaccinated people that arises when most of a group is resistant” is the definition of
o: Isolation
Herd immunity
Quarantine
Reservoir
items.s: Herd immunity is the indirect protection of unvaccinated people that arises when most of a group is resistant.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “sickness arising from eating or drinking something contaminated with organisms, toxins or chemicals”
o: Balanced diet
Micronutrient deficiency
Food fortification
Food borne illness
items.s: Food borne illness is sickness arising from eating or drinking something contaminated with organisms, toxins or chemicals.

items.q: In this course, Exclusive breastfeeding refers to
o: giving only mother's milk, with no water or other food, for the first months of life
the conscious choice by a couple of when and how many children to have
the interval between one delivery and the next conception, kept long enough for recovery
giving a measured solution of salts and sugar by mouth to replace liquid lost in diarrhoea
items.s: Exclusive breastfeeding: giving only mother's milk, with no water or other food, for the first months of life. The other options describe Oral rehydration, Birth spacing, Family planning.

items.q: In this course, Community refers to
o: a subgroup within a larger population sharing a common characteristic that lets it be reached together
a set of people sharing a place, an interest or a common identity and interacting with one another
the set of people who, by virtue of age, place or behaviour, could develop a particular condition
the branch of practice concerned with the wellbeing of a defined group in one area rather than with individual patients alone
items.s: Community: a set of people sharing a place, an interest or a common identity and interacting with one another. The other options describe Community health, Aggregate, Population at risk.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Epidemic?
o: a condition that must by law be reported to the authority as soon as it is diagnosed
a rise in cases of a condition above the level normally expected in an area
the continuous collection, analysis and feedback of data on a condition so that action can follow
the constant or predictable presence of a condition in a given place
items.s: Epidemic: a rise in cases of a condition above the level normally expected in an area. The other options describe Surveillance, Notifiable disease, Endemic.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the constant or predictable presence of a condition in a given place”
o: Endemic
Attack rate
Prevalence
Pandemic
items.s: Endemic is the constant or predictable presence of a condition in a given place.
